description: Taking an information system from a vague business need to a specified, designed and implemented solution, using both structured tools (DFDs, decision tables) and the object-oriented toolkit (use cases, UML, design patterns). Taught to the depth of a leading systems analysis and design course.
modelledOn: Shelly and Rosenblatt, Systems Analysis and Design
Dennis, Wixom and Tegarden, Systems Analysis and Design: An Object-Oriented Approach with UML
outcomes: Explain the systems development life cycle and the roles of the analyst across its phases.
Carry out a preliminary investigation and feasibility study and present a recommendation.
Elicit requirements with interviews, questionnaires, observation, document review and JAD sessions.
Model a system with data flow diagrams, a data dictionary, process descriptions, decision tables and trees, and with UML use case, class, sequence, activity and state diagrams.
Evaluate alternatives and design outputs, inputs, databases and architecture.
Plan implementation: quality assurance, documentation, installation, training, evaluation and operation.

units.title: System analysis fundamentals, the SDLC and the analyst
topics: Information systems and their components; business and system stakeholders
The SDLC: planning, analysis, design, implementation, support; waterfall, iterative, spiral, agile and their trade-offs
Structured, object-oriented and agile analysis compared
The systems analyst: skills, ethics, role in the organisation
Modelling tools and CASE tools; the course project organisation (a Ghanaian SME, school or clinic)

units.title: Systems planning and preliminary investigation
topics: Strategic planning, business case, project request and selection
Preliminary investigation: understanding the problem, scope and constraints, fact-finding, feasibility (operational, technical, economic, schedule)
Cost-benefit analysis: payback, ROI, NPV
The preliminary investigation report and presentation

units.title: Determining requirements
topics: Functional and non-functional requirements; requirements quality
Fact-finding: interviews, questionnaires, observation, document review, sampling, research
Joint application development (JAD) and rapid application development (RAD); prototyping
Object-oriented development: use cases, actors, use case diagrams and descriptions; user stories
Agile requirements and the product backlog; requirements documentation and traceability

units.title: Analysing requirements with structured tools
topics: Data flow diagrams: context diagram, level 0 and lower levels, balancing, rules
The data dictionary: data elements, flows, stores, records, processes, entities
Process descriptions: structured English, decision tables, decision trees
Logical versus physical models; entity-relationship diagrams for the data
Worked case: an admissions or billing system from interview notes to DFDs

units.title: Object-oriented analysis with UML
topics: Objects, classes, attributes, methods, messages, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism
Domain modelling and class diagrams: associations, multiplicity, aggregation, generalisation
Sequence and communication diagrams; activity diagrams; state machine diagrams
From use cases to classes: CRC cards and responsibility assignment

units.title: Evaluating alternatives
topics: Development strategies: in-house, packaged software, customisation, outsourcing, SaaS
Hardware and software evaluation; requests for proposal and quotations; benchmarking vendors
CASE tools and development environments
Feasibility revisited and the system requirements document; presenting to management

units.title: Systems design
topics: Output design: reports, screens, forms, dashboards; input design: forms, validation, controls
User interface design principles for analysts
File and database design: normalisation review, data storage, codes, data integrity and security
Architecture: client-server, web-based, cloud, mobile; processing methods; system design specification
Object-oriented design: design patterns (Observer, Factory, Strategy), package diagrams, deployment diagrams
Security and control design

units.title: Systems implementation
topics: Quality assurance: reviews, walkthroughs, inspections; testing levels; test plans
Documentation: program, system, operations, user
Installation: direct, parallel, pilot, phased changeover; data conversion; training
Post-implementation evaluation and the final report

units.title: Systems operation, support and project close
topics: Maintenance types: corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive; configuration management
Performance, capacity and system security during operation
Future trends: low-code, AI-assisted development, continuous delivery
Project presentation: the complete analysis and design package

schedule.title: Information systems and the development life cycle
schedule.exercise: Describe the components and stakeholders of a school fee-payment system, then compare waterfall, iterative and agile approaches for building it, concluding with a recommendation.

tasks.title: Draw a diagram of a clinic information system showing people, data, processes, hardware and software, and mark the five main stakeholders
Pick a development life cycle model for three different project cases, justify each choice, and score the decisions against the rubric
Advise an SME on moving from structured to object-oriented analysis for a stock system, weighing cost, skills and risk, and score the decision

schedule.title: The analyst's role and tools
schedule.exercise: Write a short profile of the skills and ethical duties of a systems analyst and pick the organisation (SME, school or clinic) for your course project with a one-paragraph description.

tasks.title: Respond to an ethical dilemma where a client asks the analyst to hide a known system weakness, and score the choices against the rubric
Create a simple project organisation chart and context sketch for your course project in the diagram studio and save it to the project folder
Compare two modelling tools by drawing the same use case diagram in each and list differences in notation support and export

schedule.title: Project selection and feasibility
schedule.exercise: Prepare a feasibility study for a mobile-money agent tracking system, covering operational, technical, economic and schedule feasibility, with payback and NPV calculations.

tasks.title: Calculate payback period and ROI for a proposed system from a table of costs and annual benefits and say whether it is worthwhile
Compute the NPV of two competing system options over five years at a 15 percent discount rate and recommend the better option
Conduct a preliminary investigation of a failing clinic records process, choosing fact-finding steps and feasibility checks, and score the report

schedule.title: Requirements and fact-finding
schedule.exercise: Write 12 requirements for a school timetable system, tag each as functional or non-functional, and rewrite three vague requirements so they are testable.

tasks.title: Sort a list of 15 statements into functional and non-functional requirements and flag the five that are ambiguous or untestable
Interview a simulated shop owner to elicit requirements for a sales system, choosing questions and follow-ups, and score the coverage
Plan and run a JAD workshop scenario with conflicting stakeholders, decide the agenda and prototype scope, and score the resolution

schedule.title: Use cases, user stories and the backlog
schedule.exercise: Write a use case description with main and alternate flows for a pharmacy stock reorder, and convert it into five user stories with acceptance criteria and priorities.

tasks.title: Draw a use case diagram with four actors and eight use cases for a library system and add include and extend relationships
Write a fully dressed use case description for registering a student including preconditions, main flow and two alternate flows
Prioritise a 20-item backlog under a fixed budget, trace each item to a requirement, and score the traceability and value order

schedule.title: Data flow diagrams and process specification
schedule.exercise: From a short interview narrative about a canteen ordering process, draw a context diagram, a level 0 diagram and a data dictionary entry for each data store.

tasks.title: Draw a context diagram for a canteen ordering system with external entities and the main data flows between them
Expand a context diagram into a balanced level 0 DFD with five processes and three stores, and check there are no black holes or miracles
Write structured English, a decision table and a decision tree for a discount policy with four conditions, and show all three agree

schedule.title: Logical models and a worked case
schedule.exercise: Turn interview notes about hospital billing into a logical DFD and an ER diagram, then explain what changes when you move to a physical design.

tasks.title: Draw an entity-relationship diagram with five entities, attributes and cardinalities for a school admissions system
Convert a physical DFD that names a particular paper form and till into a logical DFD that describes only the underlying data and processes
Model an admissions system from interview notes with a context diagram, level 0 DFD and ER diagram, and cross-check names and flows between them

schedule.title: Object-oriented modelling with UML
schedule.exercise: Identify candidate classes from a use case narrative for an online bus ticket system, assign responsibilities with CRC cards, and draw the class diagram.

tasks.title: Draw a class diagram for a library with Book, Member and Loan classes, including attributes, methods and multiplicity on each association
Draw a sequence diagram of a customer buying a bus ticket across four objects, with one alternate fragment for a failed payment
Build CRC cards for an order system, derive the class diagram, and draw a state machine for the Order class with five states

schedule.title: Development strategies and vendor evaluation
schedule.exercise: Compare in-house, packaged and SaaS options for a clinic appointment system on cost, control and risk, and draft a short request for proposal.

tasks.title: Choose between in-house, packaged, outsourced and SaaS for four cases and justify each with cost and risk, scored against the rubric
Score three vendor proposals on weighted criteria in a decision matrix and recommend a vendor, checking the result with changed weights
Present a system requirements document and recommendation to management in a scenario, responding to challenging questions, and score the outcome

schedule.title: Input, output, interface and data design
schedule.exercise: Design the input form, a monthly report and a dashboard for a school fees system with validation rules, and normalise the underlying tables to third normal form.

tasks.title: Sketch a registration form with six fields and write a validation rule and an error message for each
Normalise a given unnormalised student fees table to third normal form, create the tables, and check no data is lost with a join
Review a poorly designed screen against usability principles, choose the fixes with the best effect, and score against the heuristic rubric

schedule.title: Architecture, design patterns and security
schedule.exercise: Choose an architecture for a mobile-money agent app on poor connectivity, draw its deployment diagram, and apply the Observer pattern to its notifications.

tasks.title: Draw a deployment diagram of a web-based school system with browser, web server, application server and database nodes
Draw a class diagram applying the Strategy pattern to a payment system with mobile money, card and cash methods
Select security controls for a payroll system with limited budget, defending each against the threat it addresses, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Testing, documentation and installation
schedule.exercise: Write a test plan with ten test cases for the registration use case and choose a changeover strategy for rolling the system out to 30 branches.

tasks.title: Draw the testing levels as a V-model diagram mapping each test level to the design document it verifies
Choose direct, parallel, pilot or phased changeover for three organisations, justify each choice, and score against the rubric
Run a post-implementation review of a new records system from usage and cost data, deciding recommendations, and score the final report

schedule.title: Maintenance, trends and final presentation
schedule.exercise: Assemble the full analysis and design package for your course project and prepare a ten-minute presentation covering requirements, models, architecture, testing and rollout.

tasks.title: Classify twelve change requests as corrective, adaptive, perfective or preventive maintenance and score the classifications against the rubric
Respond to a capacity and security incident on a live fee system by choosing monitoring actions and fixes, and score against the rubric
Produce a consistent package of use cases, class diagram, sequence diagram and DFD for one project and check that the names agree across all of them
